species: rat (Sprague-Dawley, primary cortical neuron culture); mouse (GAD2-Cre/tdTomato, brain slices)
readout_other: GCaMP6f calcium imaging (wide-field fluorescence); whole-cell patch-clamp recording (current-clamp and voltage-clamp) in brain slices
direction_notes: TFOE optoacoustic stimulation evoked calcium transients/action potentials in cultured neurons and excitatory pyramidal cells; inhibitory interneurons showed subthreshold depolarization at rest and required additional depolarizing current to reach threshold for a short action potential train.
safety_notes: Tip-surface temperature during a 50 ms/7.8 mW stimulation train increased by only 0.093 +/- 0.004 degC and was undetectable for the 1 ms/11.4 mW condition, both far below the reported threshold for thermal-induced neuron modulation.

exposures.label: Single-cell / subcellular TFOE stimulation of cultured primary cortical neurons (calcium imaging)

timing.protocol_description: A TFOE was placed ~5 um from a targeted neuron. Laser pulse trains at 1030 nm, 1.7 kHz repetition rate, of either 50 ms duration (7.8 mW, 85 pulses) or 1 ms duration (two pulses, 11.4 mW) were delivered to evoke calcium transients. Separately, single-laser-pulse (3 ns) stimulation was used to test threshold pulse energy (1-8 pulses) and to demonstrate sub-microsecond acoustic pulses as the shortest stimuli reported for neuron activation.

exposures.label: TFOE stimulation of neurons in acute mouse cortical brain slices with whole-cell patch-clamp recording

timing.protocol_description: TFOE was integrated with a patch pipette and placed ~5-10 um from GAD2-tdTomato-negative pyramidal neurons or GAD2-tdTomato-positive inhibitory interneurons in mouse cortical slices; laser pulse trains of 1030 nm, 11.4 mW, 1.7 kHz repetition rate and 5 ms duration were used while recording membrane voltage under current-clamp.

flags.reason: Value (Laser: 11.4 mW, 1.7 kHz, 5 ms duration) is stated only in a figure caption (Fig. 5), not in the main running text describing the patch-clamp experiment.

2.7 MPa is the headline device characterization (measured in water at the emitter tip, ~0 um distance); actual pressure delivered to cells stimulated at ~5-10 um distance is lower (paper separately states 1.9 MPa at 10 um) and was not applied uniformly to every reported exposure condition.
Controls used (TTX pharmacology; uncoated bare-fiber 'laser only' control) do not map cleanly onto the closed sham_type vocabulary; coded as 'other'.

This is a photoacoustic (optically-driven) ultrasound emitter applied at single-cell/tissue-slice range rather than a conventional transcranial/piezoelectric transducer study; included per batch listing.

Paper reports per-experiment sample sizes (e.g. N=6 from 3 cultures; N=8 cells from three cultures; 10 neurons tested) but never a single aggregate count of cultures/preparations used across the whole study.
